---

The official Swift library for the Tungo Platform API (`https://api.tungo.kz`): the AI accountant, 1C integration, bank statements, e-invoices, tax forms and automations of [Tungo AI](https://tungo.kz).

It is generated from the API's OpenAPI contract, so its methods and models always match the contract it was built from.

## Requirements

Swift 5.10 or newer (Swift 6 language mode is supported: every public type is `Sendable`). Platforms: macOS 12, iOS 15, tvOS 15, watchOS 8, visionOS 1 and Linux. The only dependency is [swift-crypto](https://github.com/apple/swift-crypto), which provides HMAC on Linux, Windows and Android. On Apple platforms the SDK uses CryptoKit and swift-crypto is neither compiled nor linked; Swift Package Manager still resolves it (it appears in `Package.resolved`), because a package cannot declare a dependency for some platforms only.

## Installation

Add the package to the dependencies of your `Package.swift`:

```swift
dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-swift.git", from: "0.3.0")
],
targets: [
    .target(name: "MyApp", dependencies: [.product(name: "TungoSDK", package: "tungo-sdk-swift")])
]
```

In Xcode: **File > Add Package Dependencies...** and enter `https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-swift.git`.

## Quick start

```swift
import TungoSDK

let client = TungoClient(apiKey: "tg_...", companyID: "co_...")

let reply = try await client.ask("What is the VAT on the last sale?")
print(reply.answer)
```

## Authentication and configuration

Create one client and share it: it is immutable and safe to use from several threads or tasks. Every option can be passed explicitly; five of them fall back to environment variables.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `TUNGO_API_KEY` | none |
| Base URL | `TUNGO_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tungo.kz` |
| Webhook secret | `TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | none |
| Default company | `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID` | none |
| Default workspace | `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID` | none |
| Timeout | | 60 s (600 s for non-streaming chat turns) |
| Maximum retries | | 2 |
| Default headers, HTTP client | | none, built-in |

The API key is sent only to operations that require it; public endpoints and incoming hooks never receive it, and it never appears in error messages or debug output. Calling an authenticated operation without a key fails locally, before any request is made.

Every method also accepts per-request options: timeout, maximum retries, extra headers, an idempotency key and cancellation.

```swift
// Every option is explicit; apiKey, baseURL, webhookSecret, workspaceID and companyID fall back to
// TUNGO_API_KEY, TUNGO_BASE_URL, TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET, TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID and TUNGO_COMPANY_ID.
let configuration = URLSessionConfiguration.ephemeral
configuration.httpMaximumConnectionsPerHost = 4
let client = TungoClient(
    apiKey: "tg_...",
    webhookSecret: "whsec_...",
    workspaceID: "ws_...",
    companyID: "co_...",
    timeout: 30,
    maxRetries: 3,
    defaultHeaders: ["X-App": "ledger"],
    sessionConfiguration: configuration
)

// Per-request options. Cancelling the surrounding Task cancels the request.
let options = RequestOptions(timeout: 10, maxRetries: 0, headers: ["X-Trace": "abc"], idempotencyKey: "order-1532")
let decision = try await client.proposals.approve(id: "P-000042", options: options)
print(decision)

// The HTTP status, headers, request id and rate-limit state of a call.
let response = try await client.companies.listWithResponse()
print(response.statusCode, response.requestID ?? "-", response.rateLimit?.remaining ?? -1)
```

The built-in transport owns its `URLSession` (it needs the session's delegate to stream responses), so an existing session cannot be passed in; pass its `URLSessionConfiguration` instead, or implement the one-method `TungoTransport` protocol to use another HTTP stack. Redirects are not followed. `client.close()` releases the session. The configuration you pass is copied, not changed. A negative `maxRetries` is not clamped: calls fail with `ValidationError` before anything is sent.

## Errors

Every failure is a subtype of the SDK's base error. An HTTP error response becomes an API error chosen by the `error.type` field of the response body, falling back to the HTTP status when the body is not the API's error envelope:

| `error.type` | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | 400 |
| `authentication_error` | 401 |
| `payment_required_error` | 402 |
| `permission_error` | 403 |
| `not_found_error` | 404 |
| `conflict_error` | 409 |
| `gone_error` | 410 |
| `limit_error` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500 |
| `unavailable_error` | 503 |

An API error carries the status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, the parsed retry-after delay, the response headers and the raw body. Problems that happen without a response have their own types: connection error, timeout, decode error (a successful response whose body is not valid), and configuration or validation error (raised before any request).

```swift
let client = TungoClient(apiKey: "tg_...", companyID: "co_...")
do {
    _ = try await client.proposals.get(id: "P-000042")
} catch let error as APIError where error.kind == .notFound {
    print("No such proposal:", error.localizedDescription)
} catch let error as APIError {
    // status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, retry-after, headers, raw body
    print(error.statusCode, error.type, error.code ?? "-", error.requestID ?? "-", error.retryAfter ?? 0)
    for field in error.fields {
        print(field.path, field.message)
    }
} catch let error as TimeoutError {
    print("Timed out:", error.message)
} catch let error as ConnectionError {
    print("Network problem:", error.message)
} catch let error as any TungoError {
    print("Other SDK error:", error.message)
}
```

All errors conform to `LocalizedError`: `error.localizedDescription` contains the server's message. Cancelling the task that awaits a call throws `CancellationError`.

## Retries and timeouts

A request is retried up to 2 times (3 attempts) on connection errors, timeouts and the statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, but only when repeating it is safe: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests, and `POST` or `PATCH` requests of the operations whose contract declares an `Idempotency-Key`. For those the SDK generates a random key and reuses it for every attempt; you can pass your own. Other operations send no key, not even one you pass, because the API would ignore it.

The delay between attempts is `min(0.5 s × 2^attempt, 8 s)` with random jitter. A positive `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After` response header overrides it; if the server asks for more than 60 s the SDK does not wait and raises the error with the delay filled in.

The timeout covers the whole request including reading the body. Streaming calls have no total timeout, only a connect timeout and an idle timeout of 120 s. Cancellation supplied by the caller is combined with the timeout.

```swift
// For the whole client ...
let client = TungoClient(apiKey: "tg_...", companyID: "co_...", timeout: 20, chatTimeout: 300, maxRetries: 5)

// ... or for one call.
let companies = try await client.companies.list(options: RequestOptions(timeout: 5, maxRetries: 0))
print(companies)
```

## Pagination

List operations use cursor pagination (`{ data, next_cursor }`). The plain method returns one typed page that knows whether there is a next page and can fetch it. The auto-paging variant is a lazy iterator: it requests the next page only when needed, carries your filters over, and stops fetching as soon as you stop iterating.

```swift
let client = TungoClient(apiKey: "tg_...", companyID: "co_...")

// One page at a time.
var page = try await client.proposals.list(limit: 50, status: "awaiting_approval")
print(page.data.count, page.body.total, page.hasNextPage)
while let next = try await page.nextPage() {
    page = next
}

// Every item, lazily: the next page is requested only when the loop needs it.
for try await proposal in client.proposals.listAll(status: "awaiting_approval") {
    print(proposal.id)
    if proposal.id == "P-000042" { break } // no further requests are made
}
```

A server that returns a cursor it was already asked for (the same one twice, or a cycle such as A, B, A) ends the iteration with a `PaginationError` instead of looping forever.

## Streaming

Streaming operations use server-sent events and deliver typed events as they arrive. Leaving the loop early or closing the stream closes the connection. A stream request is retried only before its first byte; an error response is raised as the same typed API error as for ordinary calls. A chat stream that ends before its final event is reported as an error, never as a finished answer.

```swift
let client = TungoClient(apiKey: "tg_...", companyID: "co_...")

let stream = try await client.chat.createStream(body: ChatMessageRequest(message: "Show the receivables for October"))
print("dialog:", stream.dialogID ?? "-", "turn:", stream.turnNo ?? 0)
for try await event in stream {
    switch event {
    case .text(let text): print(text.delta, terminator: "")
    case .tool(let tool): print("\n[tool \(tool.name): \(tool.status)]")
    case .error(let failure): print("\n[error: \(failure.error.message)]")
    case .done(let done): print("\n[done: \(done.stopReason ?? "-")]")
    default: break // other and future event types
    }
}

// Or let the SDK accumulate the turn; an error event is thrown as StreamError.
let turn = try await client.streamChat("And for November?").collect()
print(turn.text, turn.costTiyn ?? 0)
```

The three event-stream endpoints (`chat.listEvents`, `feed.listEvents`, `batches.listEvents`) return the same `EventStream`. `stream.lastEventID` is the `id` of the last event delivered; to resume a stream after a disconnect, pass it in the `Last-Event-ID` header through `RequestOptions.headers`.

Nothing is read before the first iteration and events are read one chunk at a time, on demand. Leaving the loop, `stream.cancel()` or letting go of a stream that was never iterated closes the connection. Cancelling the task that iterates makes the loop throw `CancellationError`. The built-in transport does not slow the server down: bytes that arrived but were not read yet stay in memory, so do not keep a stream open without reading it.

`collect()` throws `DecodeError` when the stream ends without its final `done` event (the partial text is in the error's `body`), so a cut connection never looks like a finished answer; the plain loop simply ends. A 2xx answer to a streaming call that is not `text/event-stream` is a `DecodeError` as well. The exception is a finished chat turn that the API replays for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (`application/json` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`): its stored result arrives as the events of that turn, ending with `done`.

## Webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are signed according to the Standard Webhooks specification (Svix). The verify helper takes the raw request body and the headers (`webhook-*` or `svix-*`), checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and the timestamp within 300 s of the system clock, and returns the typed event. Any problem is reported as a webhook verification error. If no secret is passed, the client's webhook secret is used.

The send-hook helper posts an event to an incoming hook (`/hooks/{token}`) and, when given a secret, signs the exact bytes it sends in the `X-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header. The API key is never sent to hooks.

```swift
// In your HTTP handler: pass the raw body and the request headers.
func handleWebhook(body: Data, headers: [String: String]) throws {
    let event = try TungoWebhooks.verify(body: body, headers: headers, secret: "whsec_...")
    switch event {
    case .proposalWritten(let written): print("written:", written.data.proposalID)
    case .ping: print("ping")
    default: break
    }
}

// Send an event to an incoming hook; with a secret the body is signed (X-Signature).
struct Order: Encodable {
    var id: String
    var amountTiyn: Int64
}
let client = TungoClient()
let accepted = try await client.sendHook(
    token: "th_...", payload: Order(id: "order_1532", amountTiyn: 4_500_000), secret: "hksec_...", eventID: "order_1532")
print(accepted.eventID, accepted.duplicate)
```

`client.verifyWebhook(body:headers:)` does the same with the client's webhook secret. `TungoWebhooks.verifyHookSignature(body:signature:secret:)` checks an `X-Signature` on your side. A hook created with its own `signature_header` takes the signature in that header: pass `signatureHeader: "x-my-signature"` to `sendHook` or `automations.postHook`.

## Money

The API expresses amounts in tiyn (1/100 of a tenge) as 64-bit integers. The money helper converts decimal strings and exact decimal values to tiyn without floating-point error, rounding half away from zero (`"1.005"` → `101`), and formats tiyn for display (`4500000` → `45 000,00 ₸`). Invalid input raises a typed error.

```swift
let tiyn = try TungoMoney.toTiyn("45000.50")            // 4500050
let exact = try TungoMoney.toTiyn(Decimal(string: "1.005")!)   // 101
print(TungoMoney.formatTiyn(tiyn))                       // 45 000,50 ₸
print(TungoMoney.formatTiyn(-50, currency: "USD"), exact)  // -0,50 $ 101
print(TungoKazakhstan.isValidBINOrIIN("990140000017"))   // true
```

`toTiyn` also accepts a `Double` and converts it through its shortest round-trip decimal text; prefer `String` or `Decimal` for money.

## Models

Every schema of the contract is a `Codable`, `Hashable`, `Sendable` struct or enum; nothing in the public API is `[String: Any]`.

- Enumerations conform to `TungoEnum` and have an `unknown(String)` case, so a value added to the API later never fails decoding.
- Discriminated unions (`ChatEvent`, `WebhookEvent`, ...) are enums with associated values and an `unknown(JSONValue)` case. It also receives a known variant whose payload does not match this version of the SDK, so one unexpected event never breaks a stream.
- Free-form JSON is `JSONValue`. 64-bit integers are `Int64` and are never routed through floating point.
- A request field that is optional and nullable has the type `Nullable<T>?`: `nil` omits it, `.null` sends an explicit `null`, `.value(x)` sends `x`.
- Dates stay RFC 3339 strings, exactly as the API sends them.

## Long-running operations

`client.waitForRun(id:)`, `client.runScenarioAndWait(id:)` and `client.waitForBatch(id:)` poll with a growing interval (1 s to 5 s) until the run or job finishes, and throw a `TimeoutError` of kind `.deadline` after `timeout` seconds (600 by default). Cancelling the task stops the wait.

## API reference

Generated from the Tungo Platform API contract: **13 resources, 85 methods, 22 webhook event types**.

| `client.apiKeys` | The current API key and its usage statistics | `getCurrent` · `getCurrentUsage` · `getUsage` |
| `client.webhooks` | Outgoing webhooks of an organisation (Svix): endpoints, event catalogue, deliveries and signature check | `listEndpoints / listEndpointsAll` · `createEndpoint` · `getEndpoint` · `updateEndpoint` · `deleteEndpoint` · `listEndpointAttempts / listEndpointAttemptsAll` · `rotateEndpointSecret` · `testEndpoint` · `listEventTypes` · `listMessages / listMessagesAll` · `listMessageAttempts / listMessageAttemptsAll` · `resendMessage` · `getUsage` |
| `client.chat` | Conversations with the AI accountant: questions, streaming chat (SSE), token counting and history | `list / listAll` · `create / createStream` · `countTokens` · `listMentions` · `listSuggestions` · `get` · `update` · `delete` · `answer / answerStream` · `listEvents` · `stop` |

| `client.batches` | Processing batches for bank statements, incoming e-invoices and DirectBank | `list / listAll` · `createBankStatement` · `createEsfPurchases` · `get` · `listEvents` · `stop` · `getSummary` · `listStatements / listStatementsAll` · `pollDirectbank` |

## Versioning and support

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While the major version is 0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; they are always listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-swift/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). This README describes version 0.3.0.

The code is generated: please report problems and ideas in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-swift/issues) rather than opening pull requests against generated files. To report a vulnerability, follow the [security policy](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-swift/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
